# Icon

Header: `winui/ui/media/Icon.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/Icon.hpp`.

A non-interactive icon: a symbol, a font glyph, a path, a bitmap or a picture.

It takes no input and no focus. Use it on its own or as part of a control's content, for example an icon beside a label in a [Button](button.md#uibutton). A glyph is drawn at its own size in the theme's symbol font, which is 20 DIPs for a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol). A path, a bitmap or a picture measures to its natural size and is fitted into the icon's box with its aspect ratio kept. [size()](#size) makes any of them a square of that many DIPs. A glyph, a path and a monochrome bitmap take the theme's text color unless [set_foreground()](#set_foreground) overrides it. A picture keeps its own colors. The declarative form is [`ui::Icon`](#uiicon).

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: an icon-only button.
window.set_content(ui::Button{.content = ui::Icon{.source = ui::Symbol::Accept}});

// Imperative: icon + text as a Button's content.
auto button  = std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>();
auto content = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
content->set_spacing(8.0f);
content->add(std::make_unique<ui::IconControl>(ui::Symbol::Save));
content->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Save"));
button->set_content(std::move(content));
```

## `ui::Icon`

An icon: a symbol, a font glyph, a path, a bitmap or a picture. Builds a [ui::IconControl](#uiiconcontrol).

An icon carries no text, so give it an accessible name. Set `.accessibility.decorative` instead when a label next to it already says the same thing.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing = 8,
    .content = {
        ui::Icon{ .source = ui::Symbol::Save, .accessibility = { .name = "Save" } },
        ui::Icon{ .source = ui::IconGlyph{0xE77B}, .size = 16 },
        ui::Icon{ .source = ui::IconSource::path(*ui::PathGeometry::parse("M 0,0 L 12,6 0,12 Z")) },
        ui::Icon{ .source = ui::Bitmap::read("logo.png"), .size = 32 },
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Icon{
    .source, .size, .foreground, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uiicon-source"></span>`source` | `ui::Binding<ui::IconSource>` |  | The icon: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), an [IconGlyph](../rendering/icon-glyph.md), an [ImageSource](../rendering/image-source.md), or [IconSource::path()](../rendering/icon-source.md#path)/bitmap(). |
| <span id="uiicon-size"></span>`size` | `ui::Binding<std::optional<float>>` |  | The icon's size as a square of DIPs; unset is the glyph's own size or the natural size. |
| <span id="uiicon-foreground"></span>`foreground` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | The color of a glyph, a path or a monochrome bitmap: a fixed color or a theme resource. Unset uses the theme's text color. |
| <span id="uiicon-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uiicon-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uiicon-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uiicon-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uiicon-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uiicon-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uiicon-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Icon>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::IconControl](#uiiconcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::IconControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A non-interactive icon: a symbol, a font glyph, a path, a bitmap or a picture.

It takes no input and no focus. Use it on its own or as part of a control's content, for example an icon beside a label in a [Button](button.md#uibutton). A glyph is drawn at its own size in the theme's symbol font, which is 20 DIPs for a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol). A path, a bitmap or a picture measures to its natural size and is fitted into the icon's box with its aspect ratio kept. [size()](#size) makes any of them a square of that many DIPs. A glyph, a path and a monochrome bitmap take the theme's text color unless [set_foreground()](#set_foreground) overrides it. A picture keeps its own colors. The declarative form is [`ui::Icon`](#uiicon).

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: an icon-only button.
window.set_content(ui::Button{.content = ui::Icon{.source = ui::Symbol::Accept}});

// Imperative: icon + text as a Button's content.
auto button  = std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>();
auto content = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
content->set_spacing(8.0f);
content->add(std::make_unique<ui::IconControl>(ui::Symbol::Save));
content->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Save"));
button->set_content(std::move(content));
```

### IconControl

```cpp
IconControl() = default
```

An icon with no source. It measures to nothing and draws nothing.

### IconControl

```cpp
IconControl(IconSource source)
```

An icon showing [`source`](#source).

### source

```cpp
const IconSource& source() const
```

The icon drawn. Empty by default.

### set_source

```cpp
void set_source(IconSource source)
```

Replaces the icon. Updates layout and redraws.

### size

```cpp
std::optional<float> size() const
```

The icon's size as a square of DIPs: a glyph's font size, or the square a path or picture is fitted into. nullopt (the default) is the glyph's own size, or the natural size of anything else.

### set_size

```cpp
void set_size(OptionalFloat size)
```

Sets or clears the size. Updates layout and redraws.

### foreground

```cpp
const Paint& foreground() const
```

The color of a glyph, a path or a monochrome bitmap: a fixed color or a theme resource. Unset (the default) is the theme's text color.

### set_foreground

```cpp
void set_foreground(Paint color)
```

Draws in `color` instead of the theme's text color. An empty [Paint](../tree/paint.md) goes back to the theme's color. Redraws.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

Returns true, since measuring reads only the source's size.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](../tree/element.md#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](../tree/element.md#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).
